title: Subjunctive Mastery
objectives: Master all subjunctive forms including perfect and pluperfect
Handle complex subordination with multiple subjunctives
Recognize subjunctive in various clause types

grammar.explanation: The subjunctive mood expresses doubt, potentiality, wishes, and hypothetical scenarios. Mastering the perfect and pluperfect subjunctive is essential for reading complex Latin texts.
rules: Perfect subjunctive: perfect stem + -eri- + personal endings
Pluperfect subjunctive: perfect stem + -isse- + personal endings

exercises.question: Translate: Cum venisset, omnes laeti erant.
exercises.answer: When he had come, everyone was happy.

readingPassage.latin: Cum Caesar ad Alesiam accessisset, hostes se in castra receperunt. Timebant ne a Romanis caperentur. Caesar imperavit ut milites muros facerent.
readingPassage.translation: When Caesar had approached Alesia, the enemies retreated into the camp. They feared that they might be captured by the Romans. Caesar ordered that the soldiers make walls.
notes: accessisset: pluperfect subjunctive in cum clause
caperentur: imperfect subjunctive in fear clause
